kurz: In the tightly sealed pot the pressure rises, and water only boils at around 120 °C. Those extra 20 degrees make braising meat and pulses tender about three times as fast.
bild_im_kopf: Like a lid on the boiling limit: the steam cannot escape, so the temperature keeps climbing.
was_passiert: Cooking makes steam that cannot escape from the sealed pot. The pressure rises to almost double, and with it the boiling point to around 115 to 120 °C. At this temperature connective tissue turns to gelatine much faster, and the cell walls of beans soften more quickly. There is still no browning in the pot, because everything stays moist.
warum_wichtig: A ragout in 40 instead of 120 minutes, chickpeas without hours of simmering: that saves a lot of time. Because you cannot look inside, it needs reliable times and some care.
faustregeln: For pulses: fill it only partly and add a little oil, because their foam can block the valve.
For delicate vegetables and fish: better not, because they fall apart within minutes.
Check and clean the valve and sealing ring regularly.
schritte: Brown meat first in a pan or in the open pot, because nothing browns under pressure.
Fill the pot no more than two thirds, and only half for pulses and rice.
Always add enough liquid, at least as much as the instructions say.
Close the lid, bring it up to pressure, then turn the heat down and time from the moment pressure is reached.
Let the pressure release completely before opening the lid.
